historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressants

starting.description: Peet and Behagel report an unexpected possible mood-lifting effect of mianserin in some subjects, followed by an EEG comparison and clinical investigation. Leonard recalls a route from observed sedation to EEG prediction; Fink emphasizes the EEG finding, and Itil attributes discovery of clinical antidepressant effects solely to that method. The respective contributions remain disputed. Organon later continued the tetracyclic series and selected mirtazapine as a potential anxiolytic antidepressant.

inspiration.description: Accounts variously emphasize subjective mood or sedative effects and an observed human EEG profile of the synthetic compound mianserin; the relative initiating roles are disputed.

steps.description: The 1969 human mood observation followed synthesis and testing in an anti-5-HT program.

Human EEG comparisons and subsequent pilot clinical studies investigated antidepressant potential. The institutional account describes EEG as following the mood clue; Fink and Itil give the EEG a more central role, while Leonard describes sedation before EEG prediction.
Organon continued its tetracyclic series and selected mirtazapine as a potential anxiolytic antidepressant; Pinder says that the effect on serotonin release was recognized later.
In 1982, investigators compared the 6-aza mianserin analogue Org 3770, which Pinder identifies as mirtazapine, with mianserin in pharmacological assays.
By the 1996 interview, Pinder reported that mirtazapine was approved and marketed in the United States.

design.description: Pinder retrospectively describes an earlier anti-allergy structural design using cyproheptadine and phenbenzamine as ideas. Researchers then investigated the compound's observed central effects, and continued the tetracyclic chemical series to select the 6-aza analogue mirtazapine for antidepressant development. The earlier anti-allergy design was not itself shown to be de novo antidepressant design.

circumstances.description: The mood-related observation was unexpected within the original anti-5-HT program; the subsequent EEG and clinical investigations were planned.

limits: Pinder's first-person recollection concerns selection of mirtazapine after he joined Organon in 1977; his description of the earlier mianserin observation is retrospective.
The record covers this specified lineage, not every antidepressant with serotonergic effects.
conflicts: Pinder locates the mood observations in an asthma hospital study. Peet and Behagel describe an asthma pilot, then a mood observation in an Irish study without stating the latter's indication; whether these are the same study is unresolved.

Itil's abstract attributes discovery of clinical antidepressant effects solely to quantitative EEG; Peet and Behagel credit an earlier subjective mood clue and Pinder credits both. The abstract may distinguish established effects from an early impression, so its interpretation and relative credit remain unresolved.
Peet and Behagel name amitriptyline as the EEG comparator, while Leonard names imipramine; the accounts do not establish whether they refer to the same specific comparison.
gaps: The underlying 1969 study, exact participant population and observations have not been independently identified or read; these accounts are retrospective.
The 1982 comparative pharmacology paper was read at summary extent only.
The 1972 Itil original report is located but unread, and the 1983 Itil review was read only as an abstract; these limits affect resolution of the EEG and clinical-clue disagreement.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: One account describes mood improvement during clinical use of mianserin.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: A competing origin account emphasizes EEG findings; the dossier does not settle the clinical causal bridge.
